correctness.rationale: In a finite-dimensional real Banach space the admissible pairs x,y∈S with ||x−y||=1 form a nonempty compact set (dimension≥2), so TG=2 is attained if supremum equals 2. Triangle bounds each ||x+y|| and ||x+(x−y)|| by 2; product 4 forces both equal 2. Let u=x,v=y,w=x−y, so u=v+w and all are unit. Hahn–Banach support functionals for u+v and u+w give norm-one f,g with f(u)=f(v)=g(u)=g(w)=1. Conversely these relations force admissibility and both norms exactly 2, hence TG=2. For N(s,t)=max(|s|,|t|,|s−t|), u=(1,1),v=(1,0),w=(0,1) and f(s,t)=s,g(s,t)=t satisfy all exact equalities; N(2,1)=N(1,2)=2. Published independent Example 4 directly computes J(Day–James l_inf−l_1)=3/2<2, so this is a uniformly non-square space with TG=2. Checked exact witnesses, support norms and original publication. Scope finite dim only; no attainment assertion in arbitrary infinite dim.
residual_risks: Criterion is elementary triangle-equality characterization; scientific value rests on natural converse counterexample rather than deep complexity.
Could be an unindexed later Day–James TG computation; access/search cannot prove absence.

Elementary supporting-face argument is acknowledged as elementary rather than disguised as deep theory. No identical reverse-implication counterexample located in actual primary text.
